[Dataverse has grown from {{< var dataverse.datasets_2020 >}} datasets in 2020 to roughly {{< var dataverse.datasets_released >}} released by February 2026.]{.lede}

Dataverse, UCLA's institutional repository, which DSC operates, has grown from
{{< var dataverse.datasets_2020 >}} datasets and {{< var dataverse.downloads_2020 >}}
downloads in January 2020 to roughly **{{< var dataverse.datasets_released >}}
released datasets and over {{< var dataverse.downloads_total >}} downloads** as of February 2026
({{< var dataverse.datasets_with_drafts >}} counting drafts and restricted deposits).
This is the same hosting commitment the Library made in the 2014 transfer ("necessary
technological infrastructure for continued hosting of software, data, and data
analysis tools"), grown considerably since.

Dataverse and the point-cloud server run on AWS, and Redivis is a licensed platform.
Their recurring costs, along with the Archive's core memberships (<abbr class="term"
title="Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research">ICPSR</abbr>,
~$47K/year, and the Roper Center, ~$8K/year), come out of the Archive's operating fund
from the 2014 transfer, which the Library has added to as those costs grew. Norman
Powell's gift covered AWS for about two years after DSC got its own AWS account, and
University Librarian discretionary funds backed Redivis for its first two years. The
Archive's gift fund, the Data Archive Purchase Fund, pays for data instead: the L2
voter file, the LARIAC aerial imagery, and licensed English text corpora held in UCLA
Dataverse for UCLA faculty and graduate students.
